newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ZLOTY FIRMS AS BANKS CUT CURRENCY EXPOSURE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ZLOTY FIRMS AS BANKS CUT CURRENCY EXPOSURE.

text.p: The Polish zloty nearly reached seven-week highs around 3.25 percent from the parity rate on Wednesday as banks cut zloty positions to keep higher-yielding local-currency deposits over the weekend, dealers said.

They said today's currency-selling was additionally fueled by small-scale foreign entry into Polish T-bills and orders from exporters', who want to take advantage of the strong U.S. dollar on world markets.
"Players believe the central bank will not intervene ahead of a T-bill auction, so the zloty firmed amid currency-selling sentiment today," said Witold Wozniak of Deutsche Bank Polska.
The zloty closed at 3.24/3.21 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's 3.13/3.10 percent close.
It opened at 3.1200/10 to the dollar, up from 3.1290/00 on Tuesday and at 1.8082/87 to the mark, down from 1.8059/65.

Dealers said the zloty should fall slightly on Thursday as banks again lengthen positions cut today but they expected the zloty would again search for higher levels against the basket soon and test the central bank's intervention levels.
"A strong zloty is expected with potential for central bank intervention seen as early as Friday," Deutsche's Wozniak said.
At today's extra mid-week T-bill auction minimum prices were flat as expected and the treasury sold all 400 million zlotys of bills on offer.
Foreign investors bid for some $10 million of T-bills and dealers said that foreigners would likely purchase more Polish papers if the zloty fell to below three percent from parity.
On the money market overnight rates closed at 22.20/22.50 percent, a touch below opening's 22.50/22.60.
Tomorrow/next ended at 22.25/22.60 percent against opening's 22.45/22.65 percent.
